submission.justification:
Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at a threshold of 32 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of approximately 91-92% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents a significant improvement over Algorithm-L1 (~86% at 34 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (~74% at similar thresholds).

The threshold of 32 GeV was determined through systematic optimization across the allowed 20-60 GeV range. Testing revealed that efficiency peaks in the 30-33 GeV range, with 32 GeV providing robust performance in the center of this optimal region.

All three candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget per the candidate specifications document. Algorithm-L2 is listed as a viable candidate, confirming it meets the hard latency constraint of 4.0 μs required by the front-end buffer limitations. The 2025 simulation summary also demonstrates successful prior implementation of Algorithm-L2.

This recommendation maximizes signal efficiency while satisfying all technical constraints, making it the optimal choice for the Level-1 trigger implementation.
